aspects.says: Integration tests send a real message through a mux to the transaction manager, and Wiremock stands in for the external service over real HTTP.
aspects.reason: both need a live channel or an HTTP server on a port, and a graded run has no network

aspects.says: A participant that calls an external service is tested with that service mocked, so each verdict, and the calls it should and should not receive, can be set up and checked without a network.
A participant is unit-tested on its own by handing prepare a fresh Context and checking both its answer and what it left in the context, for good input and for each kind of bad input.
A performance test fires many concurrent requests at the server and measures transactions per second.
aspects.reason: it measures wall-clock throughput against a live server, which a graded offline run cannot rely on
